target.title: Add gateway lifecycle telemetry
target.body:
Additional instructions **MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed.
## What Problem This Solves When the Windows tray cannot establish or maintain its gateway connection, existing diagnostics do not clearly show whether time is being spent preparing locally, establishing the WebSocket transport, completing the gateway handshake, or waiting for the Windows node role to become ready. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds opt-in gateway lifecycle traces, metrics, and allowlisted structured logs through the existing tray-owned OpenTelemetry exporter. Instrumentation remains observational, exports only finite operational states, and does not change connection lifecycle decisions or introduce OpenTelemetry SDK dependencies into shared libraries. ## User Impact Developers and operators with an OpenTelemetry endpoint configured can diagnose operator connection timing, reconnect attempts, authentication or pairing failures, and ready/degraded state transitions. Telemetry remains disabled when no endpoint is configured. ## Evidence - Live OTLP observation showed operator connection state logs progressing from operator connecting/node idle, through node connecting, to overall ready. - The operator root trace showed coarse child spans for preparation, WebSocket transport, and gateway handshake. - A deterministic regression test covers the reviewed race where an older queued state could otherwise export after a newer directly-sent state. - Full current-head build and local test projects passed with no failures. ## Change Type - [ ] Bug fix - [x] Feature - [ ] Refactor - [x] Docs or instructions - [x] Tests or validation - [ ] Security hardening - [ ] Chore or infrastructure ## Scope - [ ] Tray or WinUI UX - [ ] Windows node capability - [ ] Local MCP or `winnode` - [x] Gateway, connection, or pairing - [ ] Setup or onboarding - [x] Permissions, privacy, or security - [x] Tests, CI, or docs ## Validation - `.\build.ps1` — passed; Shared, CLI, WinNode CLI, SetupEngine, and WinUI built successfully for ARM64. - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests\OpenClaw.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 2,756 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed. - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests\OpenClaw.Tray.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 1,709 passed, 0 failed. - `dotnet test .\tests\OpenClaw.Connection.Tests\OpenClaw.Connection.Tests.csproj --no-restore` — 423 passed, 0 failed. - Focused ordered state-export test — 3 passed, 0 failed. - Dual-model adversarial review completed; the confirmed state-ordering race was fixed in `c3dd64c9`. ## Real Behavior Proof - Environment tested: Windows ARM64 tray with a manually configured OTLP collector/dashboard. - PR head or commit tested: `c3dd64c9` for build/tests; live collector observation was performed on `2e2de8ef` before the ordering-only follow-up. - Exact steps or command run: launched the tray, observed initial gateway connection, toggled the connection, and inspected exported logs/traces in the configured OpenTelemetry dashboard. - Evidence after fix: structured logs showed `connecting` → `connecting` → `ready`; the operator trace contained `prepare` (~1.41 s), `transport` (~88 ms), and `handshake` (~0.53 s) child spans. - Observed result: exported signals explain the staged operator/node connection and distinguish local preparation from transport and handshake time. - Screenshot or artifact links verified? (`Yes`/`No`/`N/A`): Yes - Not verified or blocked: live collector proof was not repeated after the ordering-only `c3dd64c9` follow-up; separate current-head OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP collector captures are not attached. ### Screenshots #### Operator-Gateway Connection Trace of operator connecting to gateway Trace of operator failing to connect to gateway Trace of operator reconnecting to gateway Structured logs documenting connection status changes ## Security Impact - New permissions or capabilities? (`Yes`/`No`): No - Secrets or tokens handling changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No - New or changed network calls? (`Yes`/`No`): No; signals use the existing user-configured OTLP exporter. - Command or tool execution surface changed? (`Yes`/`No`): No - Data access scope changed? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes; opt-in export now includes finite gateway lifecycle states and durations. - If any answer is `Yes`, explain the risk and mitigation: exported fields are restricted to role, operation, outcome, coarse error category, and finite operator/node/overall states. Gateway URLs and IDs, device IDs, request IDs, credentials, raw errors, and diagnostic text are excluded. ## Compatibility and Migration - Backward compatible? (`Yes`/`No`): Yes - Config or environment changes? (`Yes`/`No`): No - Migration needed? (`Yes`/`No`): No - If yes, list the exact upgrade steps: N/A ## Review Conversations - [ ] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation addressed by this PR. - [ ] I left unresolved only conversations that still need maintainer judgment.
